授業科目の概要.授業科目に関する特筆事項:
Overview of the Course
This course acts as an introduction to general sociolinguistics, while looking to the Japanese language to provide specific examples of the theories and phenomena discussed. Familiarity with the language will help follow the material, but is not required, as explanation in English will be provided for all examples. The course differs from a language class in that the goal for the students will not be to demonstrate a practical proficiency in Japanese, and little attention will be given to elements of language that permit a straightforward “correct/incorrect” evaluation. Instead, we will focus on the variation in (Japanese) language that follows the differences between its users as individuals and social groups, as well as on the ambiguous but important “gray areas” about which even native speakers may not completely agree.
Note that the particulars of the class schedule and assignments may be subject to change. Please check your email and the notice boards in the International Student Center.

授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.授業科目の目的（日本語）:
Learning Objectives
1) Gaining awareness of how various sociological factors (age, gender, ethnicity, social status,
etc.) influence language, and how – working in the reverse direction – people’s language
use provides clues to their social background.
2) Learning about Japanese values and norms, as well as the social structure, by analyzing how
they are reflected in the Japanese language.
3) Being able to apply the concepts learned in class to one’s own linguistic and cultural
background and to compare the findings with the characteristics of Japan.

授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.履修条件:
Glass Requirements:
・The class will involve a discussion of cultural values which differ from one another,
sometimes significantly. The students are expected to show basic respect for other cultures
and the opinions of other students in conversation.
・Please be punctual when coming to class and complete your assignments on time. Failure to
do so may result in a reduction of the final grade.
・Plagiarism and cheating are a breach of academic ethics and as such are strictly forbidden.
Be very careful when using the work of others in your assignments. Make sure to give credit
where it is due and clearly distinguish between your own ideas and the ideas of others.
Plagiarism is unacceptable even if it is unintentional.
・ Some use of AI (LLMs) is permitted, for instance when searching for information. However,
remember that the answers it provides may be incorrect. Furthermore, never submit text
even partially generated by AI as your own. Make an effort to think for yourself before you
consult any references, including AI.

授業科目の成績評価の方法について.備考:
Grading:
Activity in class (50%) – responding to questions posed in class, both individually and when
working in groups with other students. Preparing for the class by reading assigned homework.
Written assignments (50%) – submitting assignments of sufficient length, quality and originality
before the deadline.
